result.document_summary: California AB 325 (Chapter 338, Statutes of 2025), which amends the Cartwright Act to prohibit using or distributing a common pricing algorithm in restraint of trade or through coercion, and relaxes pleading standards for Cartwright Act complaints.
result.notes: The bill is a general antitrust measure and does not mention rental housing, landlords or rents. It is recorded as an algorithmic_rent_setting rule because its definition of 'common pricing algorithm' (software using competitor data to recommend or set prices) is broad enough to reach rent-setting software, but the text itself does not say so. Approved by the Governor on October 6, 2025 with no urgency clause stated, so the California default effective date of January 1, 2026 is applied. Section 16756.1 (pleading standard) is procedural and out of scope.

rules.title: Ban on use or distribution of common pricing algorithms (Cartwright Act)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm, meaning software or other technology used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, set or influence a price, as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade, or to coerce another person to adopt the algorithm's recommended price or term. The text is general and does not name rental housing.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm in California; the text does not limit it to residential rentals or specific building types.
rules.exemptions_text: The end consumer of a product or service is excluded from the definition of 'person'.
rules.interaction: Section 16729(c) states that nothing in the section impairs or limits the applicability of antitrust laws.
